# Open Lakehouse Contract (OLC)

> OLC is an open standard for data contracts that both DESCRIBE and EXECUTE a data product: schema, quality rules, personal-data handling, transformations, materialization, lineage and service levels in one YAML file, portable across engines (Spark, DuckDB, Polars) and platforms (Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, BigQuery, AWS, MotherDuck).

Before you hand a contract to anyone, check it. `olc validate <file>` checks it against the schema; `lakelogic validate <file>` checks the runtime can enforce it; `lakelogic lint <file>` reviews it for governance gaps.

## Writing a contract that validates first time

Every top-level key in its place (all optional except `version`, `info` and `model`):

```yaml
version: 1.0.0                      # the contract's own version
info:
  title: Trips
  table_name: silver_trips
  target_layer: silver               # bronze | silver | gold
source:
  type: landing                      # see source.type below
  path: landing/trips/
  format: parquet
  partition:
    format: "y_%Y/m_%m/d_%d"         # folder layout, strftime tokens
model:
  fields:
    - { name: trip_id, type: string, required: true }
    - { name: rider_email, type: string, pii: true, masking: hash }
    - { name: fare, type: float }
    - { name: updated_at, type: timestamp }
    - { name: is_deleted, type: boolean }
primary_key: [trip_id]               # TOP LEVEL: never inside materialization
transformations:
  - phase: pre
    deduplicate: { on: [trip_id], sort_by: [updated_at], order: desc }
quality:
  row_rules:
    - not_null: trip_id
    - range: { field: fare, min: 0, max: 1000 }
  dataset_rules:
    - unique: trip_id
materialization:
  strategy: merge                    # append | overwrite | merge | scd2
  format: delta
  soft_delete_column: is_deleted     # how source deletes arrive (lint DEL-001)
service_levels:
  freshness: 24h
schedule: "0 6 * * *"                # TOP LEVEL cron: not under service_levels
```

- Required top-level keys: `version`, `info`, `model`. Unknown keys are refused: the schema is closed, so a misspelled key fails validation instead of being ignored.
- `version` is the contract's own version (e.g. `1.0.0`). `info` carries at least `title`; `info.table_name` names the output table.
- `model.fields` is a list of `{name, type}` (plus optional `required`, `pii`, `sensitive`, `masking`, `description`, `rules`).
- `source.type` is one of: `landing`, `stream`, `table`, `delta`, `iceberg`, `database`, `dlt`, `sftp`.
- `source.format` is one of: `csv`, `tsv`, `json`, `ndjson`, `jsonl`, `xml`, `xlsx`, `xls`, `excel`, `fixed_width`, `avro`, `parquet`, `delta`, `iceberg`, `pdf`, `docx`, `pptx`, `html`, `image`.
- A transformation is a list item with exactly one operation: `rename`, `derive`, `lookup`, `filter`, `deduplicate`, `deduplicate_by_latest`, `select`, `drop`, `cast`, `trim`, `lower`, `upper`, `coalesce`, `split`, `explode`, `map_values`, `rollup`, `join`, `pivot`, `unpivot`, `json_extract`, `date_range_explode`, `bucket`, `date_diff`, `sql`; optional `phase: pre|post` (see Execution Order).
- `deduplicate` needs `on` (the key) AND `sort_by` (a column that DIFFERS between duplicates, normally `updated_at`) with `order: desc`; without an ordering it is refused.
- `materialization.strategy: merge|scd2` needs `primary_key`; `scd2` also needs `materialization.scd2.track_columns`.
- Quality: `quality.row_rules` (per row; a failing row is quarantined) and `quality.dataset_rules` (whole table). Shorthands: `not_null`, `accepted_values`, `range`, `regex_match`, `unique`, `null_ratio`, `row_count_between`, or `{name, sql}`.
- Personal data: tag `pii: true` and give a `masking` strategy (`hash|redact|partial|nullify`).
- `schema_policy` (`evolution`, `unknown_fields`) may be stated at the top level or under `server`.
- Iceberg tables are written through a catalog (`table:<catalog>.<namespace>.<table>`), never a path.
- YAML: `on` is a field name. Parsers that follow YAML 1.1 read a bare `on:` as `true`; OLC tools read it as the string `on`.

## Common mistakes

Found by running LLMs against this file; each one fails validation or lint:

- In a one-line field (`- { name: x, description: ... }`) a comma ends the value: quote any text that has a comma or a colon (`description: "Kept, not removed"`), or the rest becomes an unknown key.
- `primary_key` goes at the TOP LEVEL of the contract, never inside `materialization`.
- A date-partitioned landing folder is `source.partition.format` (e.g. `"y_%Y/m_%m/d_%d"`), not `source.partition_pattern`.
- Deduplicate with `deduplicate: {on: [...], sort_by: [...], order: desc}`. The older `deduplicate_by_latest` takes `key_columns` and `timestamp_column` only; prefer `deduplicate`.
- `deduplicate.on` is the business key ONLY. Never put the `sort_by` column in it: `on: [customer_id, updated_at]` makes every row its own group, so nothing is deduplicated (lint KEY-002). Write `on: [customer_id]`, `sort_by: [updated_at]`. This holds for scd2 too.
- `schedule` is a top-level cron string; `service_levels` holds `freshness` / `row_count`.
- EVERY silver or gold table loaded with `merge` or `scd2` must say how source deletes arrive: add a boolean field (e.g. `is_deleted`) and `materialization.soft_delete_column: is_deleted`. Without it, rows deleted at the source stay in the table forever (lint DEL-001). Do this even when the request does not mention deletes.
- `trim`, `lower` and `upper` take an object with `fields`, not a bare list: `trim: {fields: [full_name, email]}`, `lower: {fields: [email]}`.
- `derive` takes `field` (the column it writes) and `sql`: `derive: {field: total, sql: amount + fee}`. Not `name`.
- `rollup.aggregations` is a MAPPING of output column to expression, not a list: `rollup: {group_by: [city, day], aggregations: {revenue: SUM(fare), trips: COUNT(*)}}`.
- There is no `apiVersion`, `kind`, `spec`, `schema` or `servers` key: OLC is not ODCS or a Kubernetes resource. The top level is exactly the keys in the skeleton above.

## Example

A small, complete contract that validates (from `examples/orders.olc.yaml`):

```yaml
# Open Lakehouse Contract — a minimal, illustrative example.
#
# One human-readable file that both DESCRIBES and (in a conforming runtime) EXECUTES a
# data product: schema, quality, PII handling, lineage, and materialization. The same
# contract is portable across engines (Spark / DuckDB / Polars), table formats
# (Delta / Iceberg / DuckLake), and platforms (Databricks / Snowflake / Fabric /
# BigQuery / AWS / MotherDuck).
version: 1.0.0

info:
  title: Orders
  description: Cleaned, validated orders ready for analytics.
  table_name: orders
  target_layer: silver
  owner: data-team@example.com

# The declared shape of the data. Field-level PII + masking travel WITH the schema.
model:
  fields:
    - name: order_id
      type: integer
      required: true
      description: Primary key.
    - name: customer_email
      type: string
      required: true
      pii: true
      masking: partial
    - name: amount
      type: float
      required: true
    - name: status
      type: string
    - name: is_deleted
      type: boolean
      description: Set when the order is deleted at the source; the row is kept, marked.

primary_key: [order_id]

# Executable data-quality rules. Rows that fail are quarantined WITH the rule + reason.
quality:
  row_rules:
    - name: positive_amount
      sql: "amount > 0"
    - name: valid_email
      sql: "customer_email LIKE '%@%.%'"
  dataset_rules:
    - name: order_id_unique
      unique: order_id

# Provenance columns injected on every row.
lineage:
  enabled: true

# How fresh the table must be: a stalled feed is reported, not mistaken for success.
service_levels:
  freshness: 24h

# Where + how the result is written. Format/engine are backend choices — the contract
# is the invariant.
materialization:
  strategy: merge
  format: iceberg
  soft_delete_column: is_deleted   # a source delete marks the row instead of leaving it stale
```
